To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new model was developed and tested to predict the transient and steady state temperatures of PV cells and PV modules under different mounting geometries and environmental conditions.
a new dynamic model to predict PV temperatures was developed, which is applicable to all geographical sites and environmental conditions.
the developed model can accurately predict PV cell/module temperatures for any geographical site and under any environmental conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a novel model to predict the transient and steady state PV cell and module temperatures, taking into account the environmental conditions.

the development of a new PV temperature prediction model that is able to predict both transient and steady state PV temperature profiles, as well as the effect of the environmental conditions on the PV temperature.

the development of a dynamic model to predict the temperature profiles of a PV cell and PV module, both at transient and at steady state conditions, and taking into account the environmental conditions, namely the ambient temperature, the wind speed, the solar irradiance and the mounting geometry of the PV module.

the proposed model is the only one which is capable of predicting the transient temperature profiles, as well as the steady state ones, for both the bare cell and the PV module, under any environmental conditions.
this model can be applied for any PV cell or PV module and for any environmental conditions.
the proposed dynamic model can be applied for the prediction of both the transient and steady state temperature profiles of a PV cell or module under any environmental conditions.

the proposed model is a new, accurate, and easy to use model for the prediction of PV cell and module temperature, which is applicable to any PV cell, module, mounting geometry, and geographical site.
the proposed model is capable of predicting the PV cell and module temperatures, Tc and Tv, respectively, under any solar irradiance, ambient temperature and wind speed.
we have proposed an accurate model that predicts the temperature profiles of PV cells/modules both in transient and steady state.

the proposed model is capable of estimating the temperature of the PV cells and modules under any operating conditions and can be used for the design of cooling systems for PV cells and modules.

the model developed in this study is applicable to any PV module, regardless of its mounting geometry, and can be used for any location and environmental conditions.
